prerequisites: Contents of the lectures "Technical Informatics 1 - Computer Architecture" and "Technical Informatics 2 - Digital Technology".

learning_outcomes.text: Students are familiar with the fundamental aspects of designing complex logical circuits.
This includes understanding ASIC and FPGA architectures and corresponding workflows, as well as applying associated tools using Hardware Description Languages (HDLs).
Furthermore, students have a deep theoretical understanding of the various steps of the Hardware Reverse Engineering process and are aware of its implications.
In addition, students gain a deep understanding of various Gate-level Netlist Reverse Engineering methods through several practical projects.
Students are ideally prepared for theses in this area.

syllabus_topics: Part I: Basic Principles of VLSI Design (VLSI stands for Very-large-scale integration)
Introduction to ASIC and FPGA architectures
PCB Analysis, Delayering, and Image Processing
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the combined module examination. The grade contributes 5/150 to the B.Sc. IT Security/Information Technology [PO 22] final grade and 5/149 to the B.Sc. IT Security/Information Technology [PO 20] final grade.
